static_traits.name: Liu Ruibo
static_traits.family_status: Married, Has two children (one with autism spectrum disorder), has two dogs; spouse is supportive, but the client says it is not easy to fully open up
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with children is tense due to their Silence; relationship with spouse is fairly supportive; other social situations Not mentioned
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems experienced yet, no psychotherapy received yet; other personal medical history Not mentioned; the children's autism diagnosis has significantly affected family dynamics
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe emotions and thoughts; has self-Reflection ability but tends toward self-blame; cognitive biases such as mind reading, overgeneralization, and personalization often appear; emotional tone is guilt, sadness, and Anxiety; cooperativeness Good

basic_info.main_problem: I believe my children's Silence toward me is because they hate me, so I feel guilty and sad. These feelings began after the children were diagnosed with autism and have intensified in recent months. Now my relationships with both children have become distant; when interacting with them I always assume they do not like me, and these thoughts appear almost daily.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these thoughts have affected my relationships with my children and caused emotional distress. I want to repair the problems between us, feel closer to my children, and feel less Anxiety when facing their behaviors.
growth_experiences: The children's autism diagnosis was an important turning point: after the diagnosis, family pace and role Demands increased (therapy, daily routines and arrangements), the client felt overwhelmed, gradually interpreting the children's Silence as 'hating me/rejecting me', triggering persistent guilt and sadness, with a cycle in interactions of overexerting to get responses -- failing -- withdrawing -- guilt; although trying to spend more time with the children and searching online for advice, the negative automatic thoughts persist; the spouse is generally supportive, but the client finds it hard to fully open up about feelings.

core_beliefs: I am not loved by my children / I am not worthy of being loved

special_situations.event: When trying to play board games with the children, the younger (autism spectrum) child did not participate and stayed Silent
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the children are Silent or do not participate, it means they hate me, showing that I have failed as a parent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: First overexerting to win responses (arranging activities, trying frequently), then choosing to withdraw and give space when responses are not yet achieved
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They hate me / I am very boring / I am not a competent parent

special_situations.event: In daily interaction the children respond less than before, especially the autistic child is often silent
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the children do not respond, it must be that I did something wrong; it is my problem
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Increases time spent together and searches online for advice and methods to 'repair' the relationship
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I made them not want to talk to me, It is all my fault

special_situations.event: In daily family life, plans did not go as Anticipated, children were Silent or uncooperative
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If this interaction does not go well, it will always be like this in the future; I will never be able to build a good relationship with my children
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Treading carefully 'as if on thin ice' amid tension and frustration, trying to avoid triggering the other's Silence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This proves again that they do not want to be with me, and this situation will only get worse

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and close to the children, expects a warm, responsive connection
core_conflict.fear: Fears being rejected or hated by the children, fears being a failing parent
defense_goal: Reduces the possibility of direct rejection by withdrawing and giving space
Easing the Fear of being abandoned and worthlessness by overexerting to win responses

object_relations.self_representation: A guilty, failed parent who may be rejected at any moment
object_relations.object_representation: A silent, cold child who may reject oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores other possible Interpretations of the children's Silence or offers different perspectives
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating the children's Silence with negation of one's character and worth, believing the other is inwardly disdainful (transference: projecting inner Self-denial onto the children/others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insisting on affirmative phrasing (such as 'they just hate me'), with a certain but defensive tone; when asked for evidence, switching to listing scattered fragments or avoiding with Silence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When interactions are frustrated and children have not yet responded as Anticipated or are Silent
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Taking all the blame on oneself, believing one is unworthy or doing very poorly
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing in a self-blaming tone (such as 'It is all my fault/I am not good enough'), lowering volume, slowing speech, avoiding exploring other possible factors in the situation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When experiencing strong frustration or anger (plans disrupted, no response)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Displacing disappointment and anger toward the children into harsh self-reproach and retreat
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reducing descriptions of external conflict, emphasizing one's own inadequacy and yielding instead, expressing 'giving them space' in a restrained, lowered tone, avoiding expressing true disappointment.

manifestations: Experiencing the children's Silence as rejection and isolation, feeling distant from the children
Withdrawing when interactions are frustrated, feeling guilty and helpless
Feels support from the spouse but still finds it hard to fully open up and express inner feelings
outcomes: Parent-child relationship grows more distant, forming a vicious cycle
Lowers sense of self-acceptance and intimacy, strengthens feelings of failure

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves.
manifestations: After frustrated interaction, retreats to 'give space', turning disappointment and anger into self-blame and guilt
Controls oneself as if treading on thin ice to avoid receiving the 'cold treatment' again

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Interprets the children's silence as 'they hate me / deliberately ignore me'
Reading one's inner worthlessness as the other's negation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently blames self: 'I am a failed parent'
Daring not to express one's own needs and vulnerability, finding it hard to fully open up even with one's spouse

exception_events.target_problem: When interacting with the children, the client usually interprets the children's silence as disliking them, thus falling into self-blame and choosing to withdraw, leading to a more distant relationship.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At the most recent board game activity, the older child showed interest and joined the interaction, and the client gained some positive responses and a sense of connection.
exception_events.reason: Clue: adopting the different approach of a structured shared activity (board games), and the older child was interested in the activity at the time, so a positive interaction different from usual occurred.

positive_force: Attaches great importance to the parent-child relationship; actively seeks counseling and change
Willing to try different methods (arranging shared activities, searching online for advice)
Able to identify and question automatic thoughts in counseling, with some Reflection ability
negative_force: Cognitive biases are evident, such as mind reading, overgeneralization, and personalization
Strong self-blame and sense of failure, easily interpreting silence as rejection
Withdraws when frustrated, forming a vicious cycle of alienation and guilt
Long-term stress and burden from caring for an autistic child
Not easily fully opening up to others, reducing the possibility of seeking emotional support

target_behavior.behavior: When the child is silent, retreats and reduces interaction (accompanied by strong guilt and sadness)
antecedent: Encountering Silence or non-response when trying to interact with the children
Family plans not yet going as Anticipated, children showing non-participation
target_behavior.core_reason: The Fear of being rejected and Self-denial are activated under the drive of cognitive biases (mind reading, personalization, overgeneralization), compounded by long-term caregiving pressure
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible further rejection and feelings of failure, briefly easing Anxiety and guilt
target_behavior.consequence: Parent-child distance widens further, negative beliefs are Reinforced, forming a frustration -- withdrawal -- guilt cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Tries excessively hard to elicit the child's response (over-scheduling or frequent probing), then withdraws again after failure
antecedent: Notices the child responding less or going silent in interactions
Worrying about being given the 'cold shoulder' again
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeking external validation to hedge against the core belief 'I am a failure as a parent' and the Fear of not being loved
target_behavior.function: Gaining cues of affirmation and connection to lower insecurity
target_behavior.consequence: When the expected response is not yet received, Sense of frustration rises, triggering more self-blame and withdrawal, increasing relationship tension
